claim: The five account-phase lanes hold 282 graded claims (Bolna 57, Vapi 61, Retell 55, ElevenLabs 54, Sarvam 55; 242 observed, 23 inferred, 12 vendor-claimed, 5 unknown). Every claim carries evidence and every cited local path exists on disk.

Re-check of the Sonnet-tier lanes (decision.2026-10-20.account-mixed-tiers reverse_if): 20 decision-critical Vapi, Retell, ElevenLabs and Sarvam claims re-read against their saved raw artifacts; 19 confirmed in full, 1 confirmed on the response only (Retell RAP-10: the request body with the unknown field was not saved), 0 contradicted. 3 Bolna claims (Opus lane) also confirmed, including a code trace of the 900 ms hold. The reversal condition is not met.

Six Sarvam claims graded observed (SAC-20, SAC-22, SAC-29, SAC-45, SAC-47, SAC-49) rest only on vendor docs pages, because the Voice Agents key was refused; this synthesis treats them as vendor-claimed.

The Retell lane's report text (relayed to the main loop) cites claim ids that are shifted against its claims.json in several sections: e.g. report RAP-35 is claims RAP-34 (Indian numbers to +1), report RAP-43 is claims RAP-40 (live control), report RAP-33 is claims RAP-31 (platform voices), report RAP-19 is claims RAP-20 (disclosure). claims.json ids are authoritative; the saved report.md should be corrected or annotated.

Every vendor's root object is a single agent document that holds voice, brain, turn-taking, tools and post-call analysis; none normalises config into separate tables (ElevenLabs reads back 313 leaf settings in one JSON).

4 of 5 vendors version agents, with three incompatible semantics: Vapi publishes a new immutable version on every PATCH; ElevenLabs commits a version on every write (even a no-op) inside branches; Retell and Sarvam use draft then publish/commit, and Retell refuses edits to a published version (422). Bolna agents are unversioned in the API (PATCH merges, PUT replaces); only Bolna workflows have a CAS draft and published versions.

At 4 of 4 vendors whose API we could write to, the stored or running defaults of an API-created agent differ from the docs or from a dashboard-created agent: Bolna stores its open-source defaults (incremental_delay 900 vs docs 400; interrupt after 1 word vs docs 2); Retell's API agent lacks the AI-disclosure preset its dashboard agent has; ElevenLabs' new agent runs deepseek-v41-flash and speculative_turn true while its schema says gemini-2.5-flash and false; Vapi stores a name-only assistant with no model, voice or turn-taking fields and applies defaults at call time.

3 of the 4 writable vendors accept unknown request fields and silently drop them (Bolna 201, Retell 201, ElevenLabs 200 and commits a version); only Vapi rejects them ('property unknownKnob should not exist'). Bolna also accepted and did not persist its own documented llm_agent.routes.

The call is the centre of every data model; no vendor's API has a contact that owns consent, suppression and history. Retell's CRM contact is the closest (memory text, do_not_call) but keys on the exact phone string and stored 9000000001 as +19000000001; Sarvam has cohorts plus an org-wide DND list; Bolna, Vapi and ElevenLabs carry the person inline on each call.

Only Sarvam separates the dial attempt (30 fields: connectivity_status, failure_reason, ended_by, next_action_status, retry counters) from the conversation; the other four keep one record per dial with not-connected as a status.

None of the five APIs has a consent record, DLT/header field, 140/160/1600 series field or NCPR scrub object; calling windows are whole hours and off by default (Bolna), absolute earliest/latest dates (Vapi), one window per batch with America/Los_Angeles default (Retell), a single start time (ElevenLabs), or free-form HH:MM strings (Sarvam). None derives a window from the call's category.

Cross-call memory is live for customers at 1 of 5 (Retell: one running text brief per contact, read on and update off by default); ElevenLabs has it built behind a workspace flag (403 on our key); Bolna, Vapi and Sarvam have per-call variables and session or journey state only.

All five run an LLM judge after the call (Bolna auto-creates two hidden gpt-4.1-mini dispositions per agent; Vapi structured outputs and scorecards; Retell custom typed fields on a separate analysis model; ElevenLabs criteria and data collection on by default; Sarvam output variables and goal rules), and none feeds a judged result back into the agent automatically.

Documented agent-platform operations: Bolna 128 (96 paths, rebuilt from doc fragments, no spec file); Vapi 143 over 74 public paths, plus 246 operations over 137 paths in the public web SDK client; Retell 109 (SDK equals spec); ElevenLabs 200 of 420 under /v1/convai and /v1/speech-engine; Sarvam 68 Voice Agents operations plus 53 Model API operations. Vapi's 143 was counted by this lane from the saved spec.

Richest areas differ by vendor: ElevenLabs on config breadth, branches/merge and 65 per-agent permissions; Vapi on QA and events (simulations, scorecards, 29 webhook message types with 8 call-changing replies); Retell on live-call control (inject context, listen, take over) and contacts; Bolna on Indian telephony (trunk presets incl. Exotel and Vobiz, compliance applications) and workflow journeys with WhatsApp; Sarvam on campaign operations (retry ladder by outcome class, cohort rejects, attempt records, SQL boards) while exposing no agent authoring by REST.

What the dashboard can do but an API key cannot, by vendor: Vapi org billing, spend cap, limits and the Composer chat builder (401 / no route); Retell CSV contact import (JWT-only), export creation, billing and members; ElevenLabs key management, billing and seats (401); Sarvam all agent authoring, telephony and KB objects (dashboard/Genie/MCP only); Bolna sub-accounts (Enterprise 403). No vendor offers full dashboard parity on an API key.

Webhook signing is on at 3 of 5 (Retell HMAC by default; ElevenLabs HMAC; Vapi via an optional HMAC credential) and absent at 2 (Bolna execution webhooks, Sarvam). Retries default to none at Vapi, 3 at Retell, re-delivery on request at Sarvam. A pre-call or inbound decision hook exists in some form at all five; a per-contact predial veto only at Vapi.

Patterns the Bolna code shows that closed vendors' APIs also expose (inference, weighted by the 0.85 blind-calibration hit rate): trimming the assistant's history to what the caller heard (ElevenLabs agent_response_correction event and per-turn interrupted flag; Vapi interruption counts); speculative LLM generation at an early end of turn (Bolna Flux eager EOT; ElevenLabs speculative_turn with initiated vs irreversible generations metered apart); a cheap separate model for post-call judges (Bolna gpt-4.1-mini, Retell post_call_analysis_model, ElevenLabs analysis_llm); LLM-classified voicemail on transcript text (Bolna, Vapi providers, Retell detection_prompt, ElevenLabs system tool).

All five have a post-call processing phase between 'ended' and final: Bolna call-disconnected then completed; Retell call_ended then call_analyzed; ElevenLabs processing then done; Vapi's end-of-call-report carries analysis; Sarvam's webhook follows the attempt. A VP state machine needs the same explicit phase.

End-reason taxonomies are engineering codes keyed to providers: Vapi 638 values, Retell 39, ElevenLabs call_result 5 plus termination_reason, Bolna 12 hangup_detail values plus telephony hangup fields, Sarvam ended_by plus failure_reason. None carries a business outcome (agreed, call back, refused, wrong number, DND) as a field of its own; that lives in a custom judge if the buyer builds one.

Default turn-taking vocabularies are English at the three vendors whose defaults are readable: Bolna's accidental-interruption list and English check-in on a Hindi agent; Vapi's 22 acknowledgement and 20 interruption phrases; ElevenLabs requires interruption_ignore_terms to be filled per language by hand. Sarvam exposes only three coarse builder settings; Retell exposes backchannel_words; no stop-phrase list appeared among the knobs the lane read.

Bolna's code discards a short final transcript spoken while the agent talks unless it exactly matches its English stop list, and drops everything said during the welcome; with stored API defaults its reply cannot start sooner than about 1.4 s after the caller's last word from turn 2 on (500 ms endpointing, then a 900 ms hold timed from the final, re-traced by this lane in interruption_manager.py). Not yet measured on a call.

Turn-taking knob depth runs from fine (Vapi: wait seconds, three endpointing plans incl. a custom webhook, numWords/voiceSeconds/backoff; ElevenLabs: eagerness, timeouts, speculative turn, turn model, per-language ignore terms, soft-timeout fillers; Retell: responsiveness, interruption sensitivity, backchannel, per-node overrides; Bolna: words-to-interrupt, incremental delay, backoff, check-ins) to coarse (Sarvam: interrupt on/off, sensitivity L/M/H, eagerness 3 levels). No vendor ships a Hindi or Hinglish default lexicon.

India language and voice depth visible in the APIs: Retell 6 India locales of 63 (te-IN refused) and 6 of 300 voices with an Indian accent; Vapi 22 stock voices all English-labelled and hi-Latn refused on nova-3; ElevenLabs 7,750 shared Hindi voices but accepts its English default voice on a Hindi agent; Bolna lists 16 Hindi TTS providers with 1,280 ElevenLabs Hindi voices; Sarvam 222 job-tagged persona voices (hi 116). Catalogue size is not the gap; guided defaults are.

Failover is component-partial everywhere it is visible: Bolna fails over only the LLM (Azure provisioned to pay-as-you-go overflow) and runs its circuit breaker in shadow mode; Retell offers cross-provider TTS fallback_voice_ids; Vapi offers fallbackModels and a transcriber fallbackPlan it injected on create; ElevenLabs reroutes deprecated models by schedule without an edit. No API shows a telephony carrier failover.

Per-call typed cost lines exist at 4 of 5 (Bolna 5 lines in cents; Vapi 8 lines in USD; Retell product lines in cents per second; ElevenLabs a charging block in credits and fiat with speculative LLM generations split out); Sarvam exposes no cost, usage or balance route. None of the five groups cost by campaign or contact in its API.

Balance is readable with an API key at Bolna (wallet in cents plus concurrency) and partly at ElevenLabs (character usage); not at Vapi (org routes 401), Retell (no route) or Sarvam (no route). A spend cap settable by API key was observed at none; Vapi's cap tops out at USD 1,000/month and is dashboard-only.

Defaults that raise cost silently: ElevenLabs bursting on by default (2x price) and a server-default LLM about 2.4x the cost of its schema default (INR 1.23 vs 0.51 per minute at FX 95); Retell burst on by default (+USD 0.10/min for the whole call per its rate card); Sarvam 60-second agent pulses (a 30-s call costs INR 7.40 per connected minute at PAYG).

Public-phase all-in INR per connected Indian outbound minute (FX 95, ex GST) against what the API shows: Sarvam 3.9-7.4 by call length (60-s pulses); Bolna 6.1-8.0; ElevenLabs 8.2-8.9 via Exotel/Plivo (15.8-16.5 in burst); Retell 8.3-13.6 on a BYO Indian trunk (22-37 on Retell-managed numbers); Vapi 12.5-17.0 via Twilio. The API phase changed none of these, because no billable call was placed.

Reconstructed margins from the public phase (inferred, not measured): Bolna bundled voice 46-72% at PAYG; Vapi hosting fee about 90-98%; Retell infra line about 75-85%; ElevenLabs platform fee 82-97%; Sarvam list price 2.3-3.0x its own API list cost. Every incumbent has room to cut price toward a VP undercut.

Parity floor confirmed from at least 4 of 5 APIs: versioned agents with pinning; per-call overrides and variables; a pre-call decision hook; HTTP tools, transfer and end-call; a post-call webhook with the full record; typed per-call costs; a post-call LLM judge with typed extraction; simulated-caller tests; campaign create/status/cancel; knowledge bases; SIP/number import; an MCP server.

Places no incumbent API covers, each tied to a task VP can run: (1) contact-and-compliance layer with India-default E.164, cross-format dedupe, consent, DND/NCPR and category-derived windows on by default (task: messy 50-row CSV + window battery); (2) Hinglish turn-taking that never discards a short reply and listens during the opening (task: 'nahi/haan/ruko/bas' over the agent, 2.4 s pause); (3) the stored config is what runs: defaults materialised, unknown fields refused, voice-language checks, model-in-effect per call, disclosure on every creation path (task: create by API, read back, call, compare); (4) owned outcomes and economics: business outcome beside the engineering code, visible editable judges, cost and funnel by campaign and contact, per-second billing (task: find a failed call and why; cost of one campaign); (5) dashboard parity on the API and MCP, incl. import, export, balance and spend cap (task: chat builder sets up and runs a campaign end to end with no dashboard).

Beat (2) is a hypothesis, not yet an advantage: VP's own lab stacks still cut in on 15-42% of turns and every stack took the 2.4 s elderly pause (open.2026-10-19.turn-taking). It becomes a beat only when VP and the incumbents are scored on the same battery.

Signed webhooks, versioning, simulation tests, per-call cost lines and live-call context injection are parity (3-5 vendors each), not a wedge; parity plus undercut was rejected on 2026-10-17 and the margins above show incumbents can follow on price.

The walk-through phase needs owner-assisted logins at Vapi (email code), Retell (TOTP each login) and a Sarvam workspace key; Synthflow and SquadStack are sales-only and Exotel's voicebot access is unconfirmed. The consolidated list of dashboard items and billable battery items is in dashboard-walkthrough.json.

Leftovers from the account phase that a later phase must know about: Retell keeps one synthetic agent and engine on purpose (VP-SYNTHETIC-teardown-renewal-hinglish); ElevenLabs keeps one environment variable 'teardown_probe' that has no DELETE route; Vapi traffic-allocation rows and version history cannot be deleted by API. Bolna, Sarvam and the other Vapi/ElevenLabs probes were removed.

QA is the largest single block of Vapi's public API: 51 of its 143 operations sit under /eval (incl. simulations), /observability (scorecards) and /structured-output; ElevenLabs has 48 /v1/convai/agents operations and 15 test operations. Counted by this lane from the saved specs.
